title: Galois equivariant marked nodal alteration with birational quotients
statement:
Let $Y$ be an affine integral excellent Noetherian scheme, let $P$ be an integral excellent scheme, and let $f:P\to Y$ be proper dominant. Suppose its generic fibre is a smooth geometrically integral curve. Let $E\subset P$ be an effective Cartier divisor with finite etale generic fibre, possibly empty. There are a finite group $G$, integral excellent separated Noetherian schemes $C,Y'$, a commutative square $fa=bf'$ with $a:C\to P$ and $b:Y'\to Y$ projective alterations that are generically etale, and a $G$-equivariant projective flat finitely presented morphism $f':C\to Y'$. The group acts trivially on $P,Y$. There are a $G$-stable nowhere dense closed subset $T'\subset Y'$ and a $G$-stable effective Cartier divisor $D\subset C$ such that every geometric fibre of $f'$ is a nonempty connected curve with at worst ordinary double points, $f'$ is smooth off $T'$, $D\to Y'$ is finite etale, $D$ is in the smooth locus of $f'$, and $a^{-1}|E|\subseteq |D|\cup(f')^{-1}T'$. The action on $Y'\setminus T'$ is free. The actions on $C,Y'$ are admissible (every orbit is contained in an affine open); their finite scheme quotients $Q=C/G$ and $Y'/G$ exist and are integral excellent Noetherian. The morphisms $Q\to P$ and $Y'/G\to Y$ are proper birational. The generic fibre of $f'$ is smooth geometrically integral. An alteration means proper surjective and finite over a dense open; birational means an isomorphism on dense open subschemes; an ordinary double point has completed geometric-fibre ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. A scheme quotient has orbit-space topology and structure sheaf of invariant sections. Projectivity here is in the closed-immersion into projective-space convention; the affine base permits this form.

Conventions for the notions used here: [def-pc-scheme], [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

source.place: Expose IX Theorem 1.2 (all six clauses), printed pp. 131--132, and beginning of IX 1.4, p. 132 (admissibility, existence and excellence of quotients). The proper birational quotient conclusion is clause (iii). Finite etaleness of D follows from its properness and etaleness. The affine-base projectivity conversion is the same as in lem-trf-relative-marked-nodal-reduction.

proof.text: The scheme $P$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since $f$ is proper over the Noetherian scheme $Y$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-chow-noetherian] to $P\to Y$ and then [det-chow-projective-closed-immersions]. Take the reduced closure of the inverse image of the dense isomorphism open in the Chow scheme. Call it $P_0$, with $p:P_0\to P$. It is integral, projective over $Y$, and proper birational over $P$. On the generic fibre, $p_\eta$ is a proper birational map of integral curves: its source has dimension one by [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg], since its function field is unchanged. The smooth target $P_\eta$ is normal by [lem-sc-smooth-normal]. Thus [lem-trf-proper-birational-normal-curve-iso] makes $p_\eta$ an isomorphism.

source.place: IX 1.2, realized by the projective preparation of X Theorem 3.4 proof Step 1, p.160.

proof.text: Let $H_0$ be the schematic closure in $P_0$ of the inverse image of $E_\eta$ under the generic isomorphism. Its generic fibre is finite etale, including the empty case. Apply [lem-trf-flatification-horizontal-curve-pair] to $(P_0,H_0)\to Y$. It gives a projective-bundle birational blowup $v:S\to Y$ and strict transforms $(X,H)$ with $X$ integral, projective flat finitely presented of pure relative dimension one and $H$ finite flat finitely presented. The generic pair is still $(P_\eta,E_\eta)$; $S$ is excellent integral Noetherian. On the affine scheme $Y$, $\mathcal O_Y$ is ample: its principal affine opens are the nonvanishing loci of its sections, by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Hence [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective] makes $v$ projective in the required finite-projective-space convention.

source.place: X Theorem 3.4 proof Step 2, p.160; projectivity conversion, Stacks 087S.

proof.text: The flat pair $(X,H)/S$ now satisfies [lem-per-separable-stable-modification-flat-pair]: the generic curve is smooth geometrically integral and the generic marking is etale. Obtain a separable alteration $r:S_1\to S$ and a projective-bundle stable modification $(Z,J)$ of $(X,H)\times_S S_1$. Apply [lem-per-projective-galois-alteration-envelope] to $r$. It supplies a normal integral excellent Noetherian scheme $Y'$, a projective Galois alteration $c:Y'\to S$, a map $t:Y'\to S_1$, and $G=\operatorname{Aut}_{k(S)}L$ with $L=k(Y')$. Define $(C,D)=(Z,J)\times_{S_1}Y'$. The normal-base-change clause of the stable-modification node supplies integrality, excellence, Noetherianity, and a stable modification $m:(C,D)\to(X,H)\times_S Y'$. Its generic pair is $(P_\eta,E_\eta)\times_{k(Y)}L$.

source.place: X Theorem 3.4 proof Steps 3--4, pp.160--161; implements IX 1.2.

proof.text: Set $W=X\times_S Y'$. The maps $X\to S$ and $v:S\to Y$ are H-projective, so $S$ is H-projective over the affine scheme $Y$ and has an ample invertible sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ample-invertible]. The envelope map $c:Y'\to S$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense, hence H-projective by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective]. By [lem-pc-projective-base-change] and [lem-trf-h-projective-composition], both $W$ and $Y'$ are H-projective over the affine scheme $Y$. The scheme $W$ therefore has an ample invertible sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ample-invertible]. Apply [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective] to the projective-bundle curve map $m:C\to W$, and compose: $f':C\to Y'$ and $C\to Y$ are H-projective. Put $b=vc$, and let $a:C\to P$ be the composite through $W\to X\to P_0\to P$. This gives $fa=bf'$ by the defining maps of the pairs and fibre products.

The map $a$ is H-projective as well. Choose a closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_Y$. Since $P\to Y$ is separated, the graph of $a$ in $P\times_Y C$ is the pullback of its closed diagonal. Composing this graph with the base change of $i$ gives a closed immersion $C\hookrightarrow P\times_Y\mathbf P^n_Y=\mathbf P^n_P$ whose projection is $a$. This is exactly projectivity [def-kun-projective]; the graph and the composition are closed immersions since their defining ideal sheaves pull back and add. The same projective structures show that $C,Y'$ are separated and proper over $Y$ by [lem-pc-projective-proper].

source.place: IX 1.2(iii); explicit graph argument for the affine-base projectivity convention.

proof.text: For $g\in G$, pull $m$ back by the automorphism $g:Y'\to Y'$ and identify its target with $W$ using the action on the second factor. The result is another stable modification of $(X,H)\times_S Y'$: on geometric fibres the condition forbidding a contracted rational component with at most two special points is unchanged, by [def-trf-multipointed-curve-modification]. Apply [lem-trf-stable-modification-uniqueness-normal] over the normal integral qcqs scheme $Y'$. It supplies the unique isomorphism from this conjugate pair to $(C,D)$ over $W$. These isomorphisms give semilinear automorphisms $\rho_g$ of $(C,D)$ covering $g$. Both $\rho_g\rho_h$ and $\rho_{gh}$ are the unique isomorphism covering $gh$ and compatible with $m$, so they agree; similarly $\rho_1=1$. Thus they form a $G$-action, preserve the closed marking, and make $f'$ equivariant. The composite $a$ is invariant because $G$ acts trivially on $X,S,P_0,P,Y$.

source.place: X Theorem 3.4 proof Step 5, p.161; uniqueness, not an arbitrary choice of stable model.

proof.text: By the stable-modification statement, $f'$ is flat finitely presented of pure relative dimension one with nodal geometric fibres. Its generic curve is $P_\eta\times_{k(Y)}L$, smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2) and geometrically integral by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. The image of proper $f'$ is closed and contains the generic point of $Y'$, so $f'$ is surjective. Every geometric fibre is therefore nonempty. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-proper-component-count-lower-semicontinuous], the number $n(y)$ of geometric connected components is lower semicontinuous. If $n(y)>1$, an open neighbourhood of $y$ has $n>1$ and contains the generic point, contradicting the integral generic fibre. Hence all geometric fibres are connected.

source.place: IX 1.2(iv), nodal-curve definition; X 3.4 Step 3 and geometric connectedness.

proof.text: The marking $D$ is closed in $C$ and etale over $Y'$ by [lem-per-separable-stable-modification-flat-pair]. Thus it is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a),(c). Etaleness gives flatness, unramifiedness and local finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]; [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points] gives local quasi-finiteness. Apply [pqf-lem-proper-lqf-finite] to obtain finiteness. The relative smooth locus $U\subset C$ is open by [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular] and contains $D$. On $U/Y'$, a smooth relative curve, [lem-pc-cartier-criterion](3) makes $D$ a relative effective Cartier divisor. On $C\setminus D$ its ideal is the unit ideal. These two opens cover $C$, so $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $C$, including when empty.

The generic fibre of $C\to P$ over the generic point of $P$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(F\otimes_K L)$, where $K=k(Y)$ and $F=k(P)$. This tensor is a domain by the geometric integrality of $P_\eta$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and finite dimensional over $F$, so is a field. It is finite etale over $F$, since $L/K$ is finite separable by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale] and etaleness is preserved by base change [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](1). The generic fibre of $b$ is likewise $\operatorname{Spec}L$. Thus $a,b$ are dominant with finite generic fibres. They are proper by projectivity; [lem-weil-pbc-generic-finite-morphism-open-neighborhood] makes each finite over a dense open. Properness makes their dense images closed, hence surjective. This proves precisely the alteration convention of the statement.

source.place: IX 1.2(iii), separability and the finite-over-dense-open convention.

proof.text: For completeness, the generic etaleness just found holds on dense opens of the targets. On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ where either alteration is finite, its inverse image is affine and of finite presentation because $A$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-spec-limit-affine-neighbourhoods] (1)--(3), the affine open neighbourhoods of the generic point $\xi$ of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ form a directed inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transition maps, whose limit is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A,\xi}=\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Frac}A$. The base change of the finite map to this limit is its generic fibre, etale by Step 9. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-etale] with $S_0=Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $X_0$ the inverse image: the map is etale over some affine open neighbourhood of $\xi$, which is a dense open. In particular both $a$ and $b$ are generically etale. No degree-prime-to-anything assertion is used.

By [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular], the nonsmooth locus of $f'$ is closed. Its image $T_{\mathrm{sing}}$ under proper $f'$ is closed and omits the generic point, because the generic curve is smooth. Put $A=a^{-1}|E|$. This is closed in the Noetherian scheme $C$, so has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. On the generic fibre $A$ is exactly $|D|$, by the generic isomorphism of marked pairs. Each component of $A$ dominating $Y'$ has its generic point in this fibre, hence in closed $|D|$, and lies entirely in $|D|$. Let $V$ be the union of its other components. Then $T_{\mathrm{vert}}=f'(V)$ is closed by properness and excludes the generic point. Consequently $A\subset |D|\cup(f')^{-1}T_{\mathrm{vert}}$.

source.place: IX 1.2(iv),(vi); horizontal/vertical boundary construction, X 3.4 Step 8.

proof.text: The envelope node supplies a dense open $U_S\subset S$ on which $c$ is a finite etale $G$-torsor; in particular its action is free there. Its complement pulls back to a closed nowhere dense set $T_{\mathrm{free}}$ in $Y'$. Let $T'$ be the union of all $G$-translates of $T_{\mathrm{free}}\cup T_{\mathrm{sing}}\cup T_{\mathrm{vert}}$. This finite union is closed, $G$-stable, and omits the generic point of integral $Y'$, hence is nowhere dense. It contains the three original bad sets, so $f'$ is smooth off $T'$, the action on $Y'\setminus T'$ is free, and $a^{-1}|E|\subset |D|\cup(f')^{-1}T'$.

source.place: IX 1.2(ii),(iv),(vi), including enlargement of the bad set, pp.131--132.

proof.text: The schemes $C,Y'$ are integral excellent Noetherian by Step 3. Step 5 proves that their morphisms to $Y$ are proper, hence separated and of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus separatedness holds over the very base $S=Y$ required in [lem-per-admissible-quotient-generic-degree]. Both are projective over the affine excellent Noetherian scheme $Y$, and their actions are over $Y$. Apply [lem-per-admissible-quotient-generic-degree]: its projective-over-affine clause makes both actions admissible. They are generically free, since the action on the dense open $Y'\setminus T'$ is free and $f'$ is equivariant and surjective. The same node now gives finite surjective scheme quotients $q_C:C\to Q=C/G$ and $q_Y:Y'\to B=Y'/G$, with invariant structure sheaves and orbit-space topology; $Q,B$ are integral excellent Noetherian of finite type over $Y$. Invariance of $a,b$ gives morphisms $\alpha:Q\to P$ and $\beta:B\to Y$.

source.place: IX 1.4 first paragraph, pp.132--133; apply the quotient theorem only with its finite-type-over-excellent-affine hypothesis.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-admissible-finite-quotient-separated] over $Y$ to the two finite quotients: $Q$ and $B$ are separated over $Y$. For any base change $Y_0\to Y$, a closed subset of $Q\times_Y Y_0$ has closed inverse image in $C\times_Y Y_0$; its image in $Y_0$ is closed because $C\to Y$ is proper, and is the same image because the finite surjection stays surjective after base change. Thus $Q\to Y$ is universally closed, and similarly $B\to Y$. Together with finite type and separatedness this is properness by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For $\alpha:Q\to P$, the graph is closed since $P/Y$ is separated; its projection to $P$ is a base change of proper $Q\to Y$. Hence $\alpha$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a)--(c), as is $\beta$.

source.place: IX 1.2(iii),1.4; properness of the induced quotient maps.

proof.text: The quotient theorem [lem-per-admissible-quotient-generic-degree] identifies the function fields of $Q,B$ with the invariant fields in $k(C),L$. On the generic marked pair the lifted action is the canonical one on the $L$ factor, by uniqueness in Step 6. The algebra $F\otimes_K L$ of Step 9 is already a field, so equals $k(C)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-field-extension-galois-invariants] with $A=F$, $M=L$: its invariant algebra is exactly $F$. Likewise $L^G=K$ by the envelope node. Thus $k(Q)=F=k(P)$ and $k(B)=K=k(Y)$ under $\alpha,\beta$. They are dominant proper maps with one-point generic fibres, so [lem-weil-pbc-generic-finite-morphism-open-neighborhood] makes them finite over dense opens.

source.place: IX 1.2(iii): the generic quotient is the original generic point, including the total-space quotient.

proof.text: Finally a finite dominant map of integral schemes inducing equality of function fields is an isomorphism after shrinking the target. Indeed take a nonempty affine open in the finite locus, with coordinate domain $A_0$; its preimage has coordinate domain $B_0$, finite over $A_0$, and both sit in the same fraction field. Choose finitely many $A_0$-module generators $b_i$ of $B_0$ and write each as $u_i/v_i$ with $u_i,v_i\in A_0$, $v_i\ne0$. After inverting $s=\prod_i v_i$, one has $(B_0)_s=(A_0)_s$. The corresponding nonempty principal open is the required dense isomorphism open. Apply this to $\alpha$ and $\beta$ of Step 15. They are proper birational in exactly the statement's convention. This concludes all clauses with the same $G,C,Y',D,T',a,b,f'$.

source.place: IX 1.2(iii), passage from equality of generic function fields to dense isomorphism opens.

proof_origin.place: IX 1.2 and beginning of IX 1.4, implemented by the preparatory Steps 1--5 and boundary Step 8 of X Theorem 3.4; generic invariant-field and affine-local projectivity arguments written out.
